core_obligations: Give the first proof: the thickening is a proper surjective finite presentation morphism with X x_{X'} X = X, so the sheaf property for the h covering {X -> X'} applies (proof lines 11267-11274).
Present the alternative proof through the empty blowup and the almost blowup square with singleton values on the empty scheme (proof lines 11276-11289).
difficulty_reason: For a sheaf F on one of the big h sites (Sch/S)_h and a morphism X -> X' which is a thickening and of finite presentation, the lemma asserts that F(X') -> F(X) is bijective (statement lines 11258-11265). The first proof observes that X -> X' is proper, surjective and of finite presentation with X x_{X'} X = X, and applies the sheaf property for the h covering {X -> X'} from Lemma labelled lemma-surjective-proper-finite-presentation-h, which is complete and is the proof that matters (proof lines 11267-11274). The author then offers a second, self-described silly proof: the blowup of X' in X is empty because the affine blowup algebra A[I/a] vanishes for nilpotent a, which is marked 'Details omitted'; this produces an almost blowup square with empty top entries, and since F of the empty scheme is a singleton, Lemma labelled lemma-blow-up-square-h gives the conclusion (proof lines 11276-11289). Recognising a finite presentation thickening as a covering of the relevant shape is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the omitted detail belongs to the alternative proof and is recorded verbatim in the editorial notes.
